work.title: Movement & rehabilitation
work.summary: Motion-capture data for gait and fall-risk research.
story: I've been a student researcher with gait rehabilitation research teams since March 2026. I help during participant sessions while people walk through the motion-capture room, then label markers, organize trials, and check the data before analysis.

I also fixed a MATLAB gait-analysis workflow that had been ported to Python: unit mismatches, gait event detection, and making it error out instead of returning a wrong number. I checked it against representative trials before handing it off.
work.role: Data preparation, Vicon labeling and analysis tooling, quality control, and participant-session support.
work.evidence: Research records and software for motion-capture preprocessing, feature extraction and review; work connected to the Clinical Rehabilitation and Biomechanics / Gait Rehabilitation research teams.
work.limitations: My part of a team project; the clinical questions and results belong to the lab.

work.title: Independent AI systems research
work.summary: My own experiments running AI models on real tasks and checking how they did.
story: I build setups where one or several AI models do real tasks, then check what they got right, where they failed, and whether adding more models was worth it.
Every run saves the task, what the models did, and what went wrong, so the result can be checked later instead of taken on trust.
work.role: Experimental design, software and system construction, execution studies, failure analysis, and reproducibility.
work.evidence: Versioned experiments, execution receipts, evaluator results, failure records, and reusable tooling developed outside formal coursework.
work.limitations: Independent work, outside school and any lab, and not peer reviewed.

work.title: CaptureSuite
work.summary: Windows software that records a multi-sensor research session into one sealed package.
story: I lead the architecture and direction of CaptureSuite. It runs a recording session across several devices and outputs one sealed package, instead of separate files from separate programs.

A daemon owns the clock and session state. Each device runs as a worker plugin in C++ or Python. There's a PySide6 operator UI, a simulator so it can be developed without hardware, and analysis jobs for quality checks and features.
The quality-check engine runs on a small synthetic session with no hardware if you want to try it.
work.role: Architecture, product direction, engineering, verification, and integration.
work.evidence: Public source describes a daemon, plugin contracts, a PySide6 operator interface, simulated capture, and downstream analysis workflows.
work.limitations: Windows-only for now. The repository is the place for setup, licensing and current limits.

work.title: Cosplay & physical making

story: I cosplay as tornadocos. I model armor and props in Blender and 3D print parts.
I keep an archive of armor, prop and print files; not all of them are finished builds. Finished work goes on Instagram.

work.evidence: An existing cosplay account and a working archive of armor, prop, Blender and 3D-printing files.

work.title: Surgical ergonomics
work.summary: Motion tracking and sensor data for a study of surgeon ergonomics in urologic surgery.
story: I contributed to a research collaboration on surgeon ergonomics in urologic surgery.
I built video-based motion-tracking workflows and helped capture and analyze EMG, heart-rate and motion-sensor data.
work.role: Development of video-based motion-tracking workflows and support for physiological and sensor data capture and analysis.
work.evidence: Collaborative urologic-surgery ergonomics work involving video, EMG, heart-rate and motion data.
work.limitations: A research collaboration, not clinical practice. No patient data or unpublished results appear here.

work.title: Proteins & molecular dynamics
work.summary: Molecular-dynamics data pipelines and physical checks on AI-generated protein structures.
story: I was a remote student researcher with the Joshi Laboratory at Georgetown from September 2025 to April 2026. Most of it was data work: finding molecular-dynamics trajectories, cleaning them, and converting them to one format.

I computed features like PCA and RMSF, and wrote checks for AI-generated protein structures (RMSD, radius of gyration, bond geometry) to catch ones that look fine and are physically wrong. I also turned papers from the field into validation plans the group could test against.
work.role: Data acquisition and standardization, structural plausibility checks, and computational-biophysics literature synthesis.
work.evidence: Project records describe trajectory handling and diagnostics including RMSD, radius of gyration, bond and geometry checks, and PCA/RMSF-style features.
work.limitations: Computational research and prototypes, not drug discovery or a biological result.

work.title: Behavior & neurobiology
work.summary: Behavioral neuroscience in the Tsai Lab at CSULB. My first lab.
story: I was in the Tsai Lab at CSULB from January to September 2025. The lab studies sex differences in brain and behavior.
I scored mouse behavior from video (automated tracking first, then checked by hand), analyzed data in GraphPad Prism, and helped with mouse handling, genotyping and tissue collection.
work.role: Behavioral video scoring with manual verification, analysis in GraphPad Prism, and laboratory support in the Tsai Lab at CSULB.
work.evidence: Research experience recorded in the CV includes behavioral observation, mouse handling, genotyping workflows and tissue-collection support.
work.limitations: Supervised work in someone else's lab; the lab's results and publications are its own.

work.title: CanvasPilot
work.summary: A Canvas CLI and MCP server that uses your normal school login instead of an API token.
story: A lot of schools don't let students create Canvas API tokens, so I built CanvasPilot to use your normal login. You sign in once in a real browser (SSO and MFA work), and a small local broker makes API calls through that session. Cookies stay in the browser profile.

It covers courses, assignments, modules, files, discussions, the calendar and more, as a CLI and as an MCP server. Tests run on fixtures, and there's an offline demo that doesn't need a Canvas account.
work.role: Software development, integration tooling, testing, and responsible-use constraints.
work.evidence: Public source documents course and assignment tools, structured digests, fixture-based tests, and a local session broker or token authentication.
work.limitations: Use it only where your school's policies allow. Submitting work and taking quizzes through it are real actions.

work.title: TowerOps
work.summary: A synthetic air-traffic decision-support demo where an agent proposes and code checks the proposal.
story: I made TowerOps for the AWS Agents for Humans challenge. It runs a synthetic scenario in which two aircraft are on a converging path. The agent can propose an advisory; it cannot issue a real clearance.

Before the simulated state changes, deterministic checks test the proposed action against the scenario and reject stale state. The demo then requires fixture approval and a matching acknowledgement, and records the result in a hash-chained audit log.
The public demo uses synthetic aircraft and fixture identities. There is no live aircraft feed, operational ATC integration or claim of aviation certification.
work.role: Prototype and software development for a public research simulation.
work.evidence: The public README, architecture note and deterministic demo describe conflict prediction, proposal checks, fixture approval/readback and audit verification.
work.limitations: Research simulation only; not operational air-traffic-control software or a real clearance system.

work.title: uma-sim
work.summary: Unofficial Umamusume career simulator, written in Rust.
story: uma-sim is my unofficial Rust engine for Umamusume's career mode: runs, events, races and scoring. It has a browser UI, a CLI, a REST API and an MCP wrapper.
Race physics is in its own clean-room crate. Tests and a calibration script check the numbers against the constants the engine loads.
work.role: Simulation design, software development, testing, and interface work.
work.evidence: Public crates, scenario and scoring code, interface packages, test instructions and licensing notices.
work.limitations: Unofficial fan software with no connection to the game's creators, and it won't match every live-game mechanic.
